create.name: Day Schildkret
create.bio:
Day Schildkret is a California artist and ritual teacher who began Morning Altars as a personal daily habit: walking out early, gathering fallen leaves, petals, stones and seeds, and arranging them on the ground into short-lived mandala-like altars that the weather then takes apart. Over time the habit became a teachable method, a seven-step practice that moves from wandering and choosing a place to creating, offering and finally letting go. He came to this after an earlier career in theatre, and much of his teaching keeps that sense of craft and gathering people together.

His work centres on marking change: endings, beginnings and the in-between times that most of us pass through without ceremony. He leads weekend retreats, online series and workshops for communities and organisations, and runs a seven-month online certification for people who want to bring nature-based ritual into their own work. He has written two books, Morning Altars, which sets out the seven steps, and Hello, Goodbye, a collection of 75 rituals for transitions of many kinds. His installations have appeared in museums, cemeteries and public gardens, and his art practice and teaching continue side by side.

books.title: Morning Altars: A 7-Step Practice to Nourish Your Spirit through Nature, Art, and Ritual
books.author: Day Schildkret
books.description: Sets out the seven steps of the Morning Altars practice, from wandering outdoors and choosing a spot to building an altar from found natural objects and leaving it to the elements. Illustrated throughout with photographs of his altars.

books.title: Hello, Goodbye: 75 Rituals for Times of Loss, Celebration, and Change
books.author: Day Schildkret
books.description: A book of simple ceremonies for life's transitions, such as moving home, ending a relationship, welcoming a child or saying farewell. Each ritual uses ordinary materials and can be done alone or with others. Foreword by Elena Brower.

courses.title: Thresholds and Altars: Nature-Based Rituals for Life's Transitions
courses.description: A weekend residential retreat at Esalen for people in the middle of a change in their lives. The group builds altars outdoors from foraged materials, writes and reflects, and works through four stages of moving across a threshold, with time to witness one another's work.

sprint.tier_evidence: Instagram @morningaltars 69K (og:description, 1 Nov 2026); Facebook /morningaltars 33,081 (og:description, 1 Nov 2026); YouTube @Dschildkret 818 (channel header, 1 Nov 2026) → ~102.9k total → luminary
flags: Tier is borderline (~103k): almost all of it is the @morningaltars Instagram and Facebook accounts, which carry his practice name rather than his own; I counted them because Morning Altars is his own one-person art and teaching practice and he posts there in his own voice. Without them he would be local_hero (an @dayschildkret Instagram with 2,922 followers exists but is not linked from his site, so not counted or linked).
Only one usable photo (YouTube avatar, a selfie); the site's bio image shows him from above with his face hidden, and Esalen shows no headshot for him.

Availability set to worldwide: his contact page says only 'California, United States' (older press places him in Richmond, East Bay) and his regular teaching is online or at venues, so no city was recorded.
His website is morningaltars.com (dayschildkret.com redirects there; www.dayschildkret.com does not resolve).

Grief is a main theme of his work (a Grief Ritual Series, grief-focused interviews); I treated grief as a life transition rather than a condition but left the grief-titled items out to be safe; a human may want to check.
left_out: Morning Altars Grief Ritual Series (online, 4/11/18 Nov 2026): grief-framed, left out as borderline under the condition rule.
